\chapter{Divergences}\label{chap:divergences}

\section*{At a glance}
\begin{itemize}
\item \lead{Source} \code{doc/DIVERGENCES.md}, rendered by \code{blueprint/scripts/render\_registers.py}; the sections below are the register's own text.
\item \lead{Entries} 20.
\end{itemize}

This register lists every place where the verification code on the \texttt{ml/\allowbreak{}verification} branch (\texttt{proof/}, library \texttt{EraseProof}), or the statements it proves, diverge from the references --- Letouzey, "A New Extraction for Coq" (TYPES 2002), and Sozeau et al., "Correct and Complete Type Checking and Certified Erasure for Coq, in Coq" (J. ACM 2025), including its MetaRocq sources at commit \texttt{4b201296} (branch 9.1). The verification follows these references as closely as the differences between Lean's kernel, as Metalean (\texttt{github.com/\allowbreak{}intgrah/\allowbreak{}metalean}, commit \texttt{9407ba4}) models it, and Rocq/PCUIC/MetaRocq allow; every place it does not, for any reason, is recorded here. Entries land with the artifact that diverges.

Each entry has an id \texttt{DV-\textless{}n\textgreater{}} and exactly these fields:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} file and declaration on the \texttt{ml/\allowbreak{}verification} branch that carries the divergence.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} the paper section/figure/theorem and the MetaRocq \texttt{file:identifier} it corresponds to.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the concrete difference between our artifact and the reference artifact.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the concrete reason the divergence is necessary --- a difference between Lean's kernel and CIC, a gap in what Metalean provides, a scope boundary of the verified fragment, or similar. This field must name a real constraint; "it was simpler" or "we chose to" is not a forcing reason.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} the alternative(s) that would have kept the divergence from existing, and why each was rejected.
\end{itemize}

An entry without a forcing reason is a defect, not a divergence: it must be removed and the statement or definition restated to match the reference instead. Differences of representation alone (a judgment in \texttt{Prop} where MetaRocq's lives in \texttt{Type}, explicit flags, bundled helpers) get no entry.

The ids numbered 1 to 22 continue those of the register of the lean4lean experiment of this repository (commit \texttt{ca56b85}), which the shipping sources and the ported definitions cite. An id whose divergence does not arise against Metalean keeps an entry that says so ("Not applicable here"), so that no citation is left without an entry; ids from 23 on are new.

\section{\texorpdfstring{Trust base}{Trust base}}\label{reg:trust-base}

What the statements and the checks rely on without proof:

\begin{itemize}
\item Lean's kernel at the pinned toolchain (\texttt{lean-toolchain}), and the axioms \texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice} and \texttt{Quot.sound}: every declaration of the library stays within them (checks C3 to C5), and its modules are replayed through the kernel (check \texttt{replay}, \texttt{leanchecker}). The replay covers the library's modules \texttt{EraseProof.*} and the shipping code's \texttt{LeanToLambdaBox.*}; the compiled \texttt{.olean} files of Metalean and Mathlib that they import are trusted as built.
\item Metalean at the pinned revision (\texttt{9407ba4}, \texttt{lake-manifest.json}, pinned in \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}spec.pin}): its typing (\texttt{Metalean.Typing}), conversion and well-formedness \leandecl{Metalean.EnvWF}, which the statements use as their notion of typing, the way MetaRocq's statements use PCUIC's. Metalean's axiom \texttt{Cardinal.exists\_\allowbreak{}inaccessibles} (its set-theoretic model) is never reached (C3).
\item Five total term builders of Metalean's translator, \leandecl{Metalean.Frontend.indTerm}, \leandecl{Metalean.Frontend.ctorTerm}, \leandecl{Metalean.Frontend.recrTerm}, \leandecl{Metalean.Frontend.wrapCase} and \leandecl{Metalean.Frontend.quotTerm} (\leanfile{Metalean/\allowbreak{}Frontend/\allowbreak{}Translate.lean}), with the constants they reach (156, none \texttt{partial}, \texttt{opaque}, \texttt{unsafe} or \texttt{implemented\_\allowbreak{}by}; check C6 exempts exactly these). The bridge \leandecl{EraseProof.TrM} (rules of \leandecl{EraseProof.SatTr}) uses them for the \ensuremath{\eta}-terms of constructors, recursors, inductive types and quotients with fewer arguments than their arity (DV-1). They shape the hypotheses \texttt{henv} and \texttt{he} of the final theorem, and, through \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasableS} in the rule \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.box}, its conclusion: a wrong builder could make the premises unsatisfiable, which the non-vacuity instances would show, or change which terms count as erasable. They are not proved correct; the rest of Metalean's frontend (its \texttt{partial} translator and loader) is not used.
\item The statement definitions themselves (\leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Statements.lean}, with \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean} and \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Target.lean}), which a reader checks against the references with the entries below; \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}spec.pin} holds a SHA-256 digest of each of them and of every definition of the library or of the shipping code they reach (check C12b). The shipping definitions among them are part of what the statements say: the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} syntax (\texttt{LBTerm}, \texttt{Program}), the configuration \leandecl{Erasure.ErasureConfig}, the view \leandecl{Erasure.EnvView}, the fuel bound \leandecl{Erasure.collectFuel}, and the helpers through which the source semantics, the relation and the bridge are defined, among them the \texttt{casesOn} recognizer \leandecl{Erasure.casesInfo?}, \leandecl{Erasure.Pure.instLevels}, \leandecl{Erasure.axiomatized}, \leandecl{Erasure.indexFields}, \leandecl{Erasure.minorArity}, \texttt{Lean.Expr.instantiate1'}, \texttt{toKername} and \texttt{mutualBlockKername}. The three functions under verification, \leandecl{Erasure.collectDeps}, \leandecl{Erasure.erasePure} and \leandecl{Erasure.eraseEntry}, are pinned by name only, and the definitions reached only through them are not pinned, so that a change to the code under verification leaves the pin unchanged while the proofs decide whether the theorems still hold.
\item The shipping view \leandecl{Erasure.EnvView.ofEnvironment} (\leanfile{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure/\allowbreak{}Collect.lean}), the environment \texttt{\#erase} reads: the final theorem assumes it agrees with the program (\texttt{hview}).
\item Lean's compiler and runtime for the shipping code. The theorems are about the logical definitions of \leandecl{Erasure.collectDeps}, \leandecl{Erasure.erasePure} and \leandecl{Erasure.eraseEntry}; \texttt{\#erase} runs their compiled code. The constants reached from \leandecl{Erasure.eraseEntry} without its \texttt{CoreM} path (\leandecl{Erasure.erase}) include 186 whose compiled code is not their logical definition (counted at this revision): 133 \texttt{@[extern]} constants (operations on \texttt{Nat}, \texttt{Int}, \texttt{Array}, \texttt{String} and \texttt{ByteArray}, \texttt{Lean.Name.beq}, \texttt{mixHash}, \texttt{panicCore}, \texttt{Lean.Expr.eqv}, \texttt{Lean.Expr.replaceImpl}), 34 with an \texttt{@[implemented\_\allowbreak{}by]} target (among them the constructors and \texttt{casesOn} of \texttt{Lean.Expr}, \texttt{Lean.Level} and \texttt{Lean.Name}, through their \texttt{\_\allowbreak{}override} implementations, and the monadic array loops), and 19 \texttt{opaque} constants, among them the \texttt{partial} shipping functions \texttt{LBTerm.isValue}, \texttt{LBTerm.inlinedSize} and \texttt{LBTerm.stripLambdas}, which compute only the inlining hints, not the program. \texttt{Lean.Expr.eqv} and \texttt{Lean.Expr.replaceImpl} are reached only in the index-field branches of \leandecl{Erasure.visitCases}, which no input that the fragment test accepts reaches (DV-26). The non-vacuity instance NV-1 is kernel-checked on the logical definitions; the compiled code is exercised on it by \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}tools/\allowbreak{}NVEmit.lean} and on the regression corpus.
\item What \texttt{\#erase} does around \leandecl{Erasure.eraseEntry}, which the theorems do not cover: the elaboration of the input and of the \texttt{config} term (\leandecl{Erasure.eraseElab}, \leanfile{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure/\allowbreak{}Command.lean}, which evaluates the configuration with \texttt{unsafe} \texttt{Lean.Elab.Term.evalTerm}), the printer \texttt{Serialize.to\_\allowbreak{}sexpr} that writes the program as an S-expression (\leanfile{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Printing.lean}, whose term printer \texttt{LBTerm.to\_\allowbreak{}sexpr} is \texttt{partial}), the \texttt{.inlinings} file built from the second component of the result (the statements ignore it), and the \texttt{.mli} signature.
\end{itemize}

\section{\texorpdfstring{Entries}{Entries}}\label{reg:entries}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-1}{DV-1}}\label{reg:dv-1}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval} evaluates and \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases} erases Lean terms (\texttt{Expr}), the eraser's input, whose types are those of their images in Metalean's syntax \leandecl{Metalean.Expr} under the bridge \leandecl{EraseProof.TrM} (with \leandecl{EraseProof.SatTr}, \leandecl{EraseProof.MLCtx} and the name table \leandecl{EraseProof.Binds}).
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} PCUIC's weak call-by-value evaluation \texttt{eval} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:231}; MC \S{}5.6) and the erasure relation \texttt{erases} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:88}; MC \S{}7.3, Fig. 18), both on PCUIC terms, the syntax PCUIC's typing judges; Letouzey \S{}3.1 (CIC terms).
\item \textbf{What differs:} the syntax that evaluates and the syntax that is typed differ. \texttt{Expr} has \texttt{let}, metadata, projections, literals, and constructors, recursors, inductive types and quotients as constants applied in spines; \leandecl{Metalean.Expr} is intrinsically scoped, inlines \texttt{let}, and has saturated nodes for inductive types, constructors (fields in Metalean's order, \leandecl{EraseProof.MetaOrderOK}), recursors and quotients. \leandecl{EraseProof.TrM} relates the two rule by rule after Metalean's translator (\leanloc{Metalean/\allowbreak{}Frontend/\allowbreak{}Translate.lean}{316-345}); a spine with fewer arguments than the node takes is related to the \ensuremath{\eta}-term of Metalean's total builders (trust base) applied to its arguments. \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval} evaluates a \texttt{let} as \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}zeta} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:241}) does, and \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases} relates a \texttt{let} to a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} \texttt{tLetIn} as \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tLetIn} does, with the binder rules taking the translation of the binder's type as a premise. A projection's levels and parameters are those of its major's type in a context that extends the context of the translation (\leandecl{EraseProof.TypedExt}), the context in which the Metalean term places the major: inside a minor premise that \texttt{wrapCase} (\leanloc{Metalean/\allowbreak{}Frontend/\allowbreak{}Translate.lean}{84}) wraps, it contains the case telescope; the translator reads them from the type it infers in the context of the translation.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the eraser consumes \texttt{Expr}, and Metalean's typing is stated on its own syntax. Metalean's translator is a \texttt{partial} function that decides projections with an unverified type inference, so it cannot be used in a statement; a relation modelled on it can. Typing the major in the context of the translation would need, after a substitution inside a wrapped minor premise, to move a typing out of the case telescope (strengthening), which Metalean does not prove; in the context where the major lives, the typing follows from the typing of the whole term by inversion. The \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} image of a \texttt{let} evaluates the value first (\texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}zeta}, \texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:134}), which no semantics on \leandecl{Metalean.Expr}, where the value is substituted, can follow.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} a source semantics on \leandecl{Metalean.Expr}, which loses the evaluation of \texttt{let} values and every term shape that the translator saturates; Metalean's translator as a function, which is \texttt{partial} (opaque to proofs) and outside the verified part of Metalean (check C6).
\end{itemize}

\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} not applicable: the gap was forced by lean4lean's lemmas on projections, which are not proved, and by its lack of inductive types; Metalean has both.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-3}{DV-3}}\label{reg:dv-3}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.ProgEnv} with \leandecl{EraseProof.IndBlock}, \leandecl{EraseProof.ConstTyped}, \leandecl{EraseProof.BindsExt} and \leandecl{EraseProof.findDecl}, the relation between a program's declarations, a newest-first list of Lean \texttt{ConstantInfo}s, and a Metalean environment with its name table; \leandecl{EraseProof.SubEnv}, and the evaluation environment \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv}, whose declarations are a sub-environment of the program in \leandecl{EraseProof.erases_correct_statement} (hypothesis \texttt{SubEnv \ensuremath{\sigma}.decls P}) and the dependency closure in \leandecl{EraseProof.erasePure_erases_statement} (\leandecl{EraseProof.evalEnvOf}\texttt{ view cfg decls}).
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} the well-formed global environment \texttt{wf\_\allowbreak{}ext} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICTyping.v:507}; MC \S{}3.6), whose declarations are a newest-first list searched by \texttt{lookup\_\allowbreak{}env} (\texttt{common/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Environment.v:483}); MetaRocq's \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}) evaluates the erased term over the erasure of the dependency closure \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}global\_\allowbreak{}deps} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:1602}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} the environment is a list of Lean declarations related, entry by entry, to a Metalean environment as Metalean's loader builds it (\leanloc{Metalean/\allowbreak{}Checker/\allowbreak{}Slow/\allowbreak{}Loader.lean}{55-139}): axioms, non-recursive definitions, theorems as opaque constants (DV-24), opaques, inductive blocks with their constructors and recursors, quotients; names are fresh, and a table maps each Lean name to its Metalean head. Each recursor's Lean type is related to Metalean's by translation and, besides, syntactically in one point: the minor premise of a constructor has \texttt{nfields + 2 * nrecFields} leading \ensuremath{\Pi}'s, one per field and per induction hypothesis (\leandecl{EraseProof.IndBlock}, field \texttt{minors}), and the major premise's type is headed by the recursor's inductive (field \texttt{recMajor}); each quotient constant has the kind of its name, and the

Lean types of \texttt{Quot}, \texttt{Quot.mk} and \texttt{Quot.lift} are an arity and \ensuremath{\Pi}-telescopes of their arities, as Lean's kernel declares them (\leandecl{EraseProof.QuotShape}). The relation-level theorem types in the environment of the whole program \texttt{P} and evaluates over a sub-environment of it.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the eraser reads Lean declarations (\leandecl{Erasure.EnvView}), while a Metalean environment \leandecl{Metalean.Env} is a list of entries typed by their signatures and addressed by position, not by name. The minor arities are the count the shipping \texttt{casesOn} recognizer reads from the recursor's Lean type (\leandecl{Erasure.minorArity}), and the translation fixes a type only up to metadata and definitional equality, so it does not fix that count. Evaluation and the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} dependencies range over the closure because a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constant is found by its kername (DV-14), and kernames are injective only where \leandecl{Erasure.collectDeps} checks it, on the closure; the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment the eraser emits holds the closure only.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} Metalean's loader itself, which is \texttt{partial} code outside the verified part of Metalean (check C6); one environment for typing and evaluation, which fails for programs whose names collide outside the closure.
\end{itemize}

\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} not applicable: in the lean4lean experiment recursive constants were in the fragment, modelled as fixpoints; Metalean has none to model.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-10}{DV-10}}\label{reg:dv-10}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}, \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.unfold?}: the source semantics unfolds definitions only; an opaque constant has no \ensuremath{\delta} rule.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:247}; MC \S{}5.6), which unfolds every constant whose declaration has a body.
\item \textbf{What differs:} a Lean \texttt{opaque} declaration has a value, and the eraser emits it as the body of its \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constant, but \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.unfold?} does not unfold it: evaluation is stuck where \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation unfolds.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} Metalean's environment keeps an opaque constant without its value (\leandecl{Metalean.Entry.opaque}, \leanloc{Metalean/\allowbreak{}Syntax/\allowbreak{}Env.lean}{21}), so unfolding it is not a definitional equality of Metalean, and the final theorem's last conjunct relates every evaluation to one.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} unfolding opaques as \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta} does, under which evaluation no longer preserves types: with \texttt{opaque c : T := t} and an axiom \texttt{f : (x : T) \ensuremath{\to} F x}, \texttt{f c : F c} would evaluate to \texttt{f t : F t}, and Metalean does not equate \texttt{F c} with \texttt{F t}.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-11}{DV-11}}\label{reg:dv-11}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.isAtom} with \leandecl{EraseProof.EvidentZero}, \leandecl{EraseProof.DeltaFree}, \leandecl{EraseProof.EvidentProp} and \leandecl{EraseProof.IsThm}, the rule \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.constAtom} and the spines \leandecl{EraseProof.AtomSpine}: the constants without a \ensuremath{\delta} rule that are values; and the premise \texttt{\ensuremath{\sigma}.isAtom c = false} of \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.const}: atoms erase only to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} PCUIC's atoms \texttt{atom} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:51}), which contain the inductive types \texttt{tInd}, and \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}atom} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:331}); a constant without a body has no rule. \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tConst} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:104}) relates every constant to its \texttt{tConst}; \texttt{tInd} erases only to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} (\texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}box}, \texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:140}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} a constant without a \ensuremath{\delta} rule (an axiom, an opaque, a theorem, an inductive type) is a value when its declared type is evidently an arity (\leandecl{Erasure.arityShape}), evidently a proposition (\leandecl{EraseProof.EvidentProp}), or it is a theorem; the spines it heads are values. Every other constant without a \ensuremath{\delta} rule is stuck.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} Lean's inductive types are constants, where PCUIC has the term \texttt{tInd}; and lemmas passed as arguments (theorems have no \ensuremath{\delta} here, DV-24) must be values, or the theorem is vacuous for every program that passes one. Atomhood is decided on declared types so that an atom's erasure, \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}, does not depend on the occurrence.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} every \ensuremath{\delta}-free constant a value: an axiom \texttt{n : Nat} would then be a value whose erasure, a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constant without a body, is not a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value; no \ensuremath{\delta}-free constant a value, under which programs that pass lemmas never evaluate.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-12}{DV-12}}\label{reg:dv-12}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv} with its field \texttt{axiomatized}, \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.unfold?}, \leandecl{EraseProof.evalEnvOf} (the shipping test \leandecl{Erasure.axiomatized}), and the remapped branch of \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasesDecl}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{eval} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:231}), whose \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta} unfolds a constant exactly when it has a body, and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}constant\_\allowbreak{}body} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:264}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} a definition that the configuration remaps to foreign code (\texttt{@[extern]} under \texttt{extern := .preferAxiom}) has a Lean value but no \ensuremath{\delta} rule, and \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasesDecl} relates it to a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} declaration without a body, a pair \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}constant\_\allowbreak{}body} excludes.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the eraser emits such a declaration as a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} axiom so that it is linked with its foreign implementation; neither Metalean nor \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} models that implementation, so the source can only leave the constant stuck, as \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} leaves the axiom.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} excluding programs that mention a remapped constant, which also excludes programs that never evaluate it.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-13}{DV-13}}\label{reg:dv-13}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.MLCtx} (with \leandecl{EraseProof.MLCtx.findF}) and the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.TrM.fvar} and \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.fvar}: the eraser's free variables, related to Metalean variables and to themselves in \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}; \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Target.lean}, \leandecl{EraseProof.hasFVar} and \leandecl{EraseProof.LenvClosed}: no body of the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment has a free variable.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} PCUIC's de Bruijn contexts and MetaRocq's \texttt{erase} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:989}), which works on de Bruijn indices; \texttt{closed\_\allowbreak{}env} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EGlobalEnv.v:181}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} the shipping traversal is locally nameless: it opens binders with free variables and closes them with \texttt{abstract} before a body is stored. The bridge and the erasure relation therefore have rules for free variables, and the closedness of the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment includes the absence of free variables.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the theorem is about the shipping traversal, which uses Lean's locally nameless \texttt{Expr} interface (\leanfile{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure/\allowbreak{}Pure.lean}); its intermediate states contain free variables, which the induction over the traversal must relate.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} a relation on closed terms only, under which no intermediate state of the traversal is related.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-14}{DV-14}}\label{reg:dv-14}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: the rule \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasesDeps.const}, indexed by the source constant \texttt{c} and finding its \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} declaration at \texttt{toKername c}; \leandecl{EraseProof.KernameInj}, the hypothesis \texttt{KernameInj \ensuremath{\sigma}.decls} of \leandecl{EraseProof.erases_correct_statement}; and \leandecl{EraseProof.BlockNamesInj}, a hypothesis of \leandecl{EraseProof.collectDeps_ok_of_statement}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}deps\_\allowbreak{}tConst} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:324}; MC \S{}7.4), where the PCUIC and the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} declaration are found at the same kername.
\item \textbf{What differs:} a Lean constant and its \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constant have different names (\texttt{toKername}), and two Lean names may have the same kername, so the rule names the source declaration it uses, and the simulation assumes that kernames are distinct on the evaluation environment.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} \texttt{toKername} (\leanfile{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}) is not injective; the fragment test rejects closures with two constants or two \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} blocks of one kername (\leandecl{Erasure.findCollision}, \leandecl{Erasure.findBlockCollision}), so the hypotheses hold on what the eraser erases.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} an injective name mangling, a shipping change that alters the output for every name with special characters, which the theorem does not need.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-16}{DV-16}}\label{reg:dv-16}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Target.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.LBEval} with \leandecl{EraseProof.lbAtom}, \leandecl{EraseProof.csubst}, \leandecl{EraseProof.closedn}, \leandecl{EraseProof.hasFVar} and \leandecl{EraseProof.LenvClosed}, on the shipping AST \texttt{LBTerm} (\leanfile{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}); \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}, \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasesDeps} on the same terms.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation \texttt{eval} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:119}) on \texttt{term} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EAst.v:29}), with \texttt{atom} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:36}), \texttt{csubst} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ECSubst.v:14}), \texttt{closedn} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ELiftSubst.v:90}) and \texttt{closed\_\allowbreak{}env} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EGlobalEnv.v:181}); \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}deps} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:306}); MC \S{}7.1.
\item \textbf{What differs:} \texttt{LBTerm} has no \texttt{tVar}, \texttt{tEvar}, \texttt{tCoFix}, \texttt{tLazy} or \texttt{tForce}, and its only primitive values are 63-bit integers, so \leandecl{EraseProof.LBEval} has no cofixpoint or \texttt{force} rule; it has a constructor \texttt{fvar} (DV-13), with no evaluation rule. \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasesDeps} has no rule for fixpoints and primitive values, which the fragment does not produce (DV-7, DV-26).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the theorem is about the eraser's output, an \texttt{LBTerm}, the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} that peregrine reads; the missing terms cannot occur in it.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} extending \texttt{LBTerm}, a shipping change no output needs; a separate transcription of \texttt{term}, which every statement would reach through a translation.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-17}{DV-17}}\label{reg:dv-17}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Statements.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement} assumes a run of \leandecl{Erasure.eraseEntry} that returns a program (\texttt{hrun}) and an evaluation of the source (\texttt{hev}); \leandecl{EraseProof.collectDeps_ok_of_statement} bounds the closure by the fragment test's fuel (\texttt{decls.length \ensuremath{\le} collectFuel}). The shipping oracle, fragment test and traversal are fuelled (\leandecl{Erasure.oracleFuel}, \leandecl{Erasure.collectFuel}, \leandecl{Erasure.travFuel}).
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's \texttt{is\_\allowbreak{}erasableb} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:894}) and \texttt{erase} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:989}; MC \S{}7.2), total under the hypothesis \texttt{NormalizationIn} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICSN.v:44}); \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}erase} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:1228}) and \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}), which hold for every input.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the final theorem is partial correctness: it says nothing about a run that fails (out of fuel, for example, an error of \texttt{\#erase} and never an output) and nothing about a source term that does not evaluate. No statement has a normalization hypothesis.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} Metalean proves neither normalization nor canonicity, so a total oracle by well-founded recursion cannot be defined from its results, and a normalization hypothesis would stand in for a theorem Metalean does not have. For the same reason the call-by-value source semantics \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval} is tied to Metalean only through definitional equality (the last conjunct of the final theorem), and nothing shows that a typed program evaluates.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} a normalization hypothesis as MetaRocq's \texttt{NormalizationIn}, which would assume what Metalean does not prove.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-23}{DV-23}}\label{reg:dv-23}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.etaSpine?} (with \leandecl{EraseProof.piInst}, \leandecl{EraseProof.lamsOf}, \leandecl{EraseProof.specialArity}), the rule \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.eta} and \leandecl{EraseProof.ShortSpine}: a constructor, recognized \texttt{casesOn}, \texttt{Quot.mk}, \texttt{Quot.lift} or recursor spine with fewer arguments than its arity evaluates to its \ensuremath{\eta}-expansion, the arguments unevaluated under the new binders; and the rule \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.eta}: such a spine erases as its \ensuremath{\eta}-expansion.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} PCUIC's \texttt{eval} evaluates the arguments of an application eagerly (\texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}app\_\allowbreak{}cong}, \texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:311}; \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}construct}, \texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:303}); MetaRocq \ensuremath{\eta}-expands constructors in \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} by a separate pass (\texttt{isEtaExp}, \texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EEtaExpanded.v:61}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} an under-applied constructor, \texttt{casesOn}, quotient or recursor spine is not a value whose arguments are values: it steps to a \ensuremath{\lambda} that keeps its arguments as they are.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the eraser \ensuremath{\eta}-expands such spines (\texttt{withAppEtaToMinArity}, \leanfile{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}), and the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value of the expansion is a closure whose arguments are not evaluated; with eager evaluation the source value has an evaluated argument where the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value has the unevaluated one, and the final theorem is false (on \texttt{P2.mk ((fun x =\textgreater{} x) B.t)}). Metalean's constructor nodes are saturated, so the bridge relates such a spine to the same \ensuremath{\eta}-expansion (DV-1).
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} PCUIC's eager evaluation, under which the final theorem is false on under-applied constructors; an \ensuremath{\eta}-expansion pass on the source before evaluation, which is not what the eraser runs.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-24}{DV-24}}\label{reg:dv-24}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.unfold?} (no \ensuremath{\delta} for theorems), \leandecl{EraseProof.IsThm} in \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.isAtom} (theorems are atoms), the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.casesProof} and \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.projProp}, and \leandecl{EraseProof.PropProj}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:247}), which unfolds a lemma like any constant with a body; \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}'s \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}iota\_\allowbreak{}sing} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:162}) and \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}proj\_\allowbreak{}prop} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:238}), which reduce a \texttt{case} or a projection on a proof erased to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}.
\item \textbf{What differs:} theorems are not unfolded, so a proof may evaluate to an atom spine instead of a constructor. A \texttt{casesOn} of a field-less \texttt{Prop} constructor on such a proof continues with the alternative (\texttt{casesProof}), and a projection of a \texttt{Prop} structure out of it is a neutral value (\texttt{projProp}). A \texttt{casesOn} on a lemma of an inductive with proof fields does not evaluate, and programs defined by well-founded recursion, whose recursion reduces only through a proof of accessibility, do not evaluate either: the final theorem holds vacuously for them, and the fragment test excludes the latter (DV-26).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} Metalean's loader adds a theorem as an opaque constant, its statement only (\leanloc{Metalean/\allowbreak{}Checker/\allowbreak{}Slow/\allowbreak{}Loader.lean}{122-127}), and \leandecl{EraseProof.ProgEnv} follows it: the value of a theorem is not translated, and typically uses recursors and tactics outside the fragment, so unfolding it has no Metalean counterpart for the last conjunct of the final theorem.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} \ensuremath{\delta} for theorems with a translated value, which excludes every program that mentions a lemma whose proof leaves the fragment.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-25}{DV-25}}\label{reg:dv-25}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.casesOn?} (the shipping recognizer \leandecl{Erasure.casesInfo?}), the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.casesIota}, \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.casesLitZero} and \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.casesLitSucc}; the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.cases} and \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.casesReduced} with \leandecl{EraseProof.CasesReduced} and \leandecl{EraseProof.FieldsErasable}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} PCUIC's \texttt{tCase}, a term, with \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}iota} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:253}); \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tCase} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:109}); \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}'s \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}iota\_\allowbreak{}sing} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:162}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} Lean has no case term: \texttt{T.casesOn} is a definition through the recursor \texttt{T.rec}. The source treats a recognized \texttt{casesOn} as primitive, without \ensuremath{\delta}, reducing on the constructor its major evaluates to; the recursor itself has no rule. A \texttt{casesOn} on a one-constructor inductive whose sort may be \texttt{Prop} erases to its alternative applied to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}s, without a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} \texttt{case} (\texttt{casesReduced}), the reduction \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}iota\_\allowbreak{}sing} makes at run time.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the eraser translates recognized \texttt{casesOn} spines to \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} \texttt{case} and never unfolds them (\leanfile{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}); a recursor it erases to a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} fixpoint of its own (DV-30), not to a \texttt{case}. The reduced form is what the eraser emits when the discriminant's sort may be \texttt{Prop}, since \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} marks a whole block as propositional or not.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} \ensuremath{\delta}-unfolding \texttt{casesOn} to \texttt{T.rec} and evaluating the recursor, which has no counterpart in the eraser's output.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-26}{DV-26}}\label{reg:dv-26}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Statements.lean}: the hypothesis \texttt{hfrag} of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement}, that the shipping fragment test \leandecl{Erasure.collectDeps} accepts the input; and \leandecl{EraseProof.collectDeps_ok_of_statement}, a sufficient condition for it (\leandecl{EraseProof.ReadClosed}, \leandecl{EraseProof.PhaseIDecl}, \leandecl{EraseProof.PlainExpr}, \leandecl{EraseProof.RecFree}, \leandecl{EraseProof.KernameInj}, \leandecl{EraseProof.BlockNamesInj}).
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}), which holds for every well-typed term.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the final theorem covers the inputs the fragment test accepts. Its exclusion classes: recursors that a read expression names other than those of a single inductive without indices that eliminates into every sort and whose induction hypotheses take no arguments and are about the last fields (\leandecl{EraseProof.RecInFragment}; \leandecl{Erasure.recShapeInFragment}), and those the eraser keeps as constants (\leandecl{Erasure.recStaysConstant}), recursive definitions (structural or well-founded: every definition with a compiled \texttt{\_\allowbreak{}unsafe\_\allowbreak{}rec} companion), \texttt{partial}, \texttt{unsafe} and \texttt{implemented\_\allowbreak{}by} constants, nested inductives, string literals, Nat literals and Nat or Int constructors under \texttt{nat := .machine}, \texttt{casesOn} on a constructor with an index field, eliminations of an inductive whose sort may be both \texttt{Prop} and not \texttt{Prop}, \texttt{remove\_\allowbreak{}irrel\_\allowbreak{}constr\_\allowbreak{}args}, metavariables. On the corpus (294 \texttt{\#erase} calls), 225 are in the fragment, 66 out (20 of them recursive definitions, one of which, \texttt{Defects.log2}, is defined by well-founded recursion) and 3 are rejected for a name collision.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} \texttt{\#erase} sends an input outside the fragment to the \texttt{Meta} path (\leandecl{Erasure.route}, \leanloc{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure/\allowbreak{}Entry.lean}{278-282}), \texttt{CoreM} code about which nothing is proved, and some of the excluded constructs have no Metalean counterpart (nested inductives, \texttt{unsafe} constants). Typed inputs outside the fragment exist, so the hypothesis cannot be derived from typing as in the lean4lean experiment.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} deriving the hypothesis from \texttt{henv}, \texttt{hview} and \texttt{he}, which is false on typed programs that use a mutual recursor; leaving the fragment unstated, which makes it impossible to tell how much the hypothesis excludes, which \texttt{collectDeps\_\allowbreak{}ok\_\allowbreak{}of} states.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-27}{DV-27}}\label{reg:dv-27}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}FirstOrder.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.FirstOrderValue}, the values on which \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_firstorder} determines the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value, and their structural erasure \leandecl{EraseProof.foErase}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{firstorder\_\allowbreak{}value} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICFirstorder.v:115}), with the first-order inductives of \texttt{firstorder\_\allowbreak{}con} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICFirstorder.v:52}), and \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct\_\allowbreak{}strong} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:2269}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} MetaRocq's first-order value is a typed constructor application of an inductive that is not propositional, every argument (parameters included) a first-order value, and its first-order inductives have neither type parameters nor proof fields. Ours is syntactic: a constructor node needs its inductive's declared sort to be never zero (\texttt{Level.isNeverZero}), and two kinds of leaves erased to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} are admitted as arguments: constructor applications of an inductive declared in \texttt{Prop}, and atom spines (type formers such as \texttt{Nat} or \texttt{List Nat} as type parameters, theorems or axioms applied to arguments as proof fields). The conclusion compares with the structural erasure, which keeps parameters (DV-23), instead of the erasure function's output.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} a Lean inductive in \texttt{Sort u} is universe-polymorphic over \texttt{Prop}: at \texttt{u := 0} its constructor applications are proofs and erase to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} or to a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constructor, so \texttt{\ensuremath{\neg} PropInductive} (Metalean's block level) does not determine the value; the declared sort being never zero does (\leandecl{EraseProof.SimInd.ctor_not_erasable}). \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} keeps parameters in constructor applications (DV-23), and Lean's data inductives take type parameters (\texttt{Prod}, \texttt{Option}, \texttt{List}) and its structures proof fields (\texttt{Subtype}, \texttt{Fin}), so MetaRocq's notion would leave only monomorphic inductives without proofs; the relation erases an atom spine in many ways (an application of an atom may erase to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} applied to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}), and only the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value restricts it to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} (\leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.atomSpine_box}). There is no erasure function on the relation's side to compare with.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} MetaRocq's notion exactly (all arguments first-order, the inductive not propositional), which is false for universe-polymorphic inductives at \texttt{Prop} and excludes every value with a type parameter; comparing with \leandecl{Erasure.erasePure}'s output, which reads the configuration and the view instead of the value alone.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-28}{DV-28}}\label{reg:dv-28}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: the rule \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasesAlt.intro} (\leanloc{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}{1167}), which \ensuremath{\eta}-introduces a \texttt{casesOn} alternative.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} the alternatives of \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tCase} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:109}), related to the erased branches by the erasure relation under the case's branch contexts; the relation has no \ensuremath{\eta}-introduction rule.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the rule \ensuremath{\eta}-introduces an alternative to the arity of its constructor, and has no premise on the alternative's shape. Before, it carried \texttt{\ensuremath{\forall} x A b bi, e \ensuremath{\ne} .lam x A b bi}, so that a \ensuremath{\lambda} alternative was related only by \texttt{ErasesAlt.lam} (peeling):

| intro : (\ensuremath{\forall} x A b bi, e \ensuremath{\ne} .lam x A b bi) \ensuremath{\to} TrM E B lps \ensuremath{\Gamma} \ensuremath{\Delta} e e' \ensuremath{\to} E[\ensuremath{\Gamma}] \ensuremath{\vdash} e' : .forallE A' B'' \ensuremath{\to} \ldots{} \ensuremath{\to} ErasesAlt E B lps \ensuremath{\sigma} \ensuremath{\Gamma} \ensuremath{\Delta} (k + 1) e (nm :: ns, t)

After:

| intro : TrM E B lps \ensuremath{\Gamma} \ensuremath{\Delta} e e' \ensuremath{\to} E[\ensuremath{\Gamma}] \ensuremath{\vdash} e' : .forallE A' B'' \ensuremath{\to} \ldots{} \ensuremath{\to} ErasesAlt E B lps \ensuremath{\sigma} \ensuremath{\Gamma} \ensuremath{\Delta} (k + 1) e (nm :: ns, t)

The relation is more permissive: a \ensuremath{\lambda} alternative is also related to the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} \ensuremath{\beta}-redex \texttt{.app a' (.bvar 0)} of its peeled branch, which evaluates to the same value.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the substitution lemma \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.inst} is false with the premise. An alternative that is a variable erases by \texttt{intro} to the branch \texttt{([x], .app (.bvar (k + 1)) (.bvar 0))}; substituting a \ensuremath{\lambda} \texttt{a} for the variable gives the source alternative \texttt{a}, which only \texttt{ErasesAlt.lam} can relate, and to the erasure of its body, never to the \ensuremath{\beta}-redex \texttt{.app a' (.bvar 0)}. The substitution lemma is needed for the \ensuremath{\beta} and \ensuremath{\zeta} steps of the simulation.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} keeping the premise and restricting substitution to non-\ensuremath{\lambda} values, which excludes the \ensuremath{\beta}-redexes the simulation has to step; adding a rule that relates a \ensuremath{\lambda} alternative to the \ensuremath{\beta}-redex only under the substitution lemma's hypotheses, which is the same relation with a more complicated shape.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-29}{DV-29}}\label{reg:dv-29}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.quotMk} and \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.quotLift}; \leandecl{EraseProof.quotEvalArity} in \leandecl{EraseProof.specialArity}, so that \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.eta} and \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.eta} \ensuremath{\eta}-expand \texttt{Quot.mk} and \texttt{Quot.lift} spines with missing arguments; the quotient clauses of \leandecl{EraseProof.BlocksCong} and \leandecl{EraseProof.SpecialSpine}; the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.quotMk} and \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.quotLift}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} none: PCUIC has no primitive quotients. The closest rules are \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}beta} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:234}) and \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}construct} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:303}) of \texttt{eval}, and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tApp} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:101}) and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tConstruct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:106}) of \texttt{erases}.
\item \textbf{What differs:} Lean's quotients are primitive constants with their own reduction, the quotient \ensuremath{\iota} \texttt{Quot.lift f h (Quot.mk r a) \ensuremath{\leadsto} f a} (\texttt{quotIota}, \leanloc{Metalean/\allowbreak{}Syntax/\allowbreak{}Reduction.lean}{74}). The source evaluates \texttt{Quot.mk \ensuremath{\alpha} r a} by evaluating the element \texttt{a}, the type and the relation unevaluated, and \texttt{Quot.lift \ensuremath{\alpha} r \ensuremath{\beta} f h q} by evaluating \texttt{f} to a \ensuremath{\lambda} and \texttt{q} to \texttt{Quot.mk \ensuremath{\alpha}' r' a} and continuing with the \ensuremath{\lambda}'s body at \texttt{a}; spines with fewer arguments are \ensuremath{\eta}-expanded as constructor spines are (DV-23), and a \texttt{Quot.mk} value blocks application congruence as a constructor value does. The erasure represents a quotient by its elements: \texttt{Quot.mk \ensuremath{\alpha} r a} erases as \texttt{a} and \texttt{Quot.lift \ensuremath{\alpha} r \ensuremath{\beta} f h q} as \texttt{f q}, applied to the erasures of the arguments beyond the arity.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the reference has no rule for quotients, and the eraser erases the quotient constants in this way, as Lean's code generator does (\texttt{visitConstApp}, \leanloc{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}{949}). The source rule is Metalean's quotient \ensuremath{\iota}, which the subject-reduction theorem \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.defeq} justifies through \leandecl{Metalean.WHRed.quotIota_defeq}.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} erasing \texttt{Quot.mk} and \texttt{Quot.lift} to \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} axioms, under which every program that computes through a quotient is stuck in \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}; no source rule for quotients, under which such programs do not evaluate and the final theorem says nothing about them.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-30}{DV-30}}\label{reg:dv-30}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: the rule \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.recIota}; the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.recLet} and \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.recFix} with \leandecl{EraseProof.RecFixOf}, \leandecl{EraseProof.recMembers}, \leandecl{EraseProof.recLets} and \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.recBlock?}; the recursor clause of \leandecl{EraseProof.SpecialSpine}; the recursor exclusion of \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.const}; the recursor clause of \leandecl{EraseProof.specialArity}; the clauses \leandecl{EraseProof.IndBlock.recIHs} and \leandecl{EraseProof.IndBlock.recMajor}; \leandecl{EraseProof.RecInFragment} in \leandecl{EraseProof.PhaseIDecl}; \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Target.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.lbLift} and \leandecl{EraseProof.LBFixed}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} none: PCUIC has no recursors (eliminators are \texttt{tCase} and \texttt{tFix}). The closest rules are \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}fix} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:273}), \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}zeta} and \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}iota} of \texttt{eval}, and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tFix} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:122}), \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tLetIn} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:96}) and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tCase} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:109}) of \texttt{erases}.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the source evaluates a saturated recursor \texttt{T.rec ps ms mins maj} of a single inductive \texttt{T} without indices, whose recursive fields take no arguments and come after the other fields of their constructor, by evaluating the minors to \texttt{mvs} and the major to a constructor value \texttt{C qs fs}, then each induction hypothesis \texttt{T.rec ps ms mvs f} (one per recursive field \texttt{f}, in the order of the minor's hypotheses) to a value, and continuing with the minor's value applied to the fields and these values. The parameters and the motive are not evaluated. There is no source \ensuremath{\iota} for recursors of mutual, nested or indexed inductives, for higher-order recursive fields, for recursive fields before non-recursive ones, nor on a \texttt{Nat} literal major (\texttt{recK} and structure \ensuremath{\eta} are not rules). Recursor spines with missing arguments are \ensuremath{\eta}-expanded, as constructor spines are (DV-23). The fragment test admits exactly the recursors of this shape that the eraser does not keep as constants (\texttt{RecInFragment}). The erasure is the eraser's: the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} fixpoint of \texttt{recFix} under \texttt{let}s of the erased minors, applied to the erased major and the extra arguments (\texttt{Erases.recLet}); \texttt{Erases.recFix} relates the same fixpoint with closed \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} values of the minors substituted, the form \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} reaches after the \texttt{let}s and in which the recursive calls appear.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the reference has no recursors, and the eraser compiles them to \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} fixpoints (\texttt{visitRec}, \leanloc{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}{1003}). \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluates the minors (\texttt{let}) and every argument of an application by value, so the source evaluates the minors and the induction hypotheses first; the restrictions make Metalean's \ensuremath{\iota} apply to the minors as they are, unwrapped by \texttt{wrapCase} (\texttt{RecWhred.orders\_\allowbreak{}identity}), which the subject-reduction theorem \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.defeq} uses through \leandecl{Metalean.WHRed.iota}. \texttt{IndBlock.recIHs} states which field each induction hypothesis of the recursor's Lean type is about, as Lean's kernel generates it; without it the pinned hypotheses do not fix that field (\texttt{ConstTyped} relates types only up to definitional equality). \texttt{IndBlock.recMajor} states that the major premise of the recursor's Lean type is of its inductive, as the kernel generates it; without it the fragment test's closure need not hold the block of a recursor it reads, which the evaluation over the closure needs.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} a source \ensuremath{\iota} on the unevaluated induction hypotheses, under which the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation of a hypothesis the minor ignores has no source counterpart; erasing recursors to \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} axioms (as \texttt{recStaysConstant} does for the excluded cases), under which every program that computes through a recursor is stuck in \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}.
\end{itemize}
